elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no affiliate-assignment right; an affiliate that is not a successor would require the other party's written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section (d) permits either party, including Customer, to assign to a successor to its business upon written notice, without requiring consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The right to assign to a successor to its business is broad enough to cover a successor resulting from an acquisition, subject only to written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: A buyer succeeding to the business through a substantially-all-assets sale falls within the stated right to assign to a successor to the business upon notice.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign to a successor to its business merely upon written notice, without Customer's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments other than assignments to a successor, Section (d) requires Customer's written consent and states that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no competitor prohibition and would permit assignment to a competitor if it is a successor or if consent is obtained.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: No termination right tied to Customer's change of control appears in the supplied operative language.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business without consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) allows either party to assign to a successor to its business upon written notice, without consent.

elements.element: Customer must provide the Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor to its business.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment right is expressly conditioned on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business without consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) grants the successor-assignment right to either party, including Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor to its business.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment right is expressly conditioned on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Any other assignment by Customer requires Vendor's written consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) states that any assignment other than one to a successor requires the other party's written consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to another assignment by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section (d) provides that the required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Any other assignment by Vendor requires Customer's written consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) states that any assignment other than one to a successor requires the other party's written consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to another assignment by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section (d) provides that the required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the fallback: both parties may assign to business successors on written notice, while all other assignments require written consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits Customer's affiliate-assignment right, allows Vendor successor assignments without consent, and contains no absolute prohibition on assignments to Customer competitors. Removing only the conflicting assignment restriction from Section (c) was necessary, while the separate restrictions on transferring, leasing, exporting, or sublicensing the Work remain effective.
